title: How Should a Male Pastor Minister to Women Well?
subtitle: On honoring, equipping, and protecting the women of the congregation, and how a male pastor leads with respect, wisdom, and clean boundaries

sections.title: The Load-Bearing Wall of the Church
sections.body:
Walk through the actual work of most congregations and follow the hands that do it. The meals that arrive after surgery. The nursery that runs. The prayer chain that never sleeps. The funeral reception that appears as if by grace. Trace it back, and most of it runs through the women of the church.

They are not the support staff of the kingdom. They are the load-bearing wall.

The early church was carried by women who funded it, hosted it, and stood at the cross when the men had scattered. Phoebe carried the letter to the Romans. The women were the first to the tomb and the first to preach the resurrection, to the apostles, who did not believe them at first. A pastor who treats the women of his church as helpers to be thanked at the end of a list has not read his own Bible carefully. Before we talk about what role women may fill, we should repent of how casually we have taken for granted the ones who already fill more of the work than we do.

sections.title: Honor Comes Before Anything Else
sections.body:
Whatever a church believes about office and order, and good people differ, the first command toward women in the church is not order. It is honor. Treat the older women as mothers, Paul told Timothy, and the younger women as sisters, in all purity.

Mothers and sisters. Not problems to be managed. Not temptations to be feared. Family.

A pastor sets the temperature of a whole church in how he speaks of women when none are in the room. If the jokes are cheap, the men will learn that women are cheap. If a woman's idea is only ever credited once a man repeats it, the women will learn where they stand and they will stop offering. So guard your tongue and guard the culture. Make a church where a woman's intelligence is expected and her gifting is spent and her dignity is assumed. The world tells women a hundred lies about their worth before breakfast. The church should be the one room where every lie is contradicted by the way she is treated.

sections.title: Equip Them, Do Not Warehouse Them
sections.body:
A woman in your church is carrying gifts the kingdom needs, and the question is whether you will help her spend them or quietly store them. Too many churches have a deep bench of women who teach brilliantly, counsel wisely, and lead capably, and who are handed coffee duty and asked to smile.

Gifting that is buried does not stay buried quietly. It curdles. It leaves.

Within whatever convictions you hold, there is enormous room you are probably not using. Women who can teach women. Women who can counsel the broken, run the mercy work, disciple the new believer, train the next generation of mothers in a faith their own mothers never gave them. Find the gifted ones and put real weight on them and then get out of the way. And listen to them in the rooms where decisions get made, because a leadership that only hears from men will be confidently wrong about half its own church. Equipping women is not a concession to the age. It is obedience to a God who poured out his Spirit on sons and on daughters.

sections.title: Clean Boundaries Protect the Vulnerable
sections.body:
A male pastor who ministers to women is handling something holy and something flammable, and pretending otherwise is how good men and trusting women get hurt. The answer is not to avoid women, which only abandons half your flock. The answer is to build a structure so clean that no one ever has to wonder.

Meet where there are windows. Loop in your wife and your team. Keep no secret that a counselor would have to keep.

The rules are not because women are dangerous. The rules are because power is, and a pastor has power that a hurting woman in his office does not. Use it to protect her, never to position yourself. Refer the long counseling cases to women who can sit with her in ways you should not. Let your texts and your time be transparent to people who would tell you the truth. The pastor who guards these boundaries is not being cold. He is being a man who has watched others fall and decided his flock will not pay for his ego. Guard the gate, and the women under your care can trust the whole house.

sections.title: The Sin the Church Keeps Hiding
sections.body:
We have to name the thing the church has too often covered. Women have been wounded in the house of God, by men in collars, and then told to keep quiet for the sake of the ministry. That is not protecting the church. That is sacrificing the daughter to defend the institution.

I have seen it handled with more concern for reputation than for the one who was harmed. I want no part of that ever again.

A pastor's job when a woman has been hurt is not to manage the optics. It is to believe her seriously, to act, to put her safety above his comfort and the church's image. The men who did the harm counted on our silence. They counted on us valuing the platform over the person. Refuse them that. The God who heard the cry of Hagar in the desert, who saw the woman bleeding twelve years, who would not let the bent woman stay bent, does not look kindly on shepherds who hide what was done to his daughters. Honor the women. Equip the women. And when one is wronged, stand with her, even when it costs you. Especially when it costs you.
